preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road (u, v) in the input must have distinct endpoints u and v within the valid intersection range [1, n].
The number of roads in the input must exactly match the given m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p <= n for p in path) and len(path) == k
preconditions.description: The path must consist of k distinct intersections, each within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(path[i] != path[j] for i in range(k) for j in range(i+1, k))
preconditions.description: All intersections in the path must be pairwise distinct.

preconditions.expression: all((path[i], path[i+1]) in roads for i in range(k-1))
preconditions.description: Each consecutive pair of intersections in the path must be connected by a one-way road.

preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and m >= n and k >= 2
preconditions.description: The constraints on n, m, and k must be satisfied: n >= 2, m >= n, and k >= 2.

postconditions.description: The output must be two integers: the minimum and maximum possible number of rebuilds during Polycarp's journey.
The minimum number of rebuilds must be non-negative, and the maximum must be at least the minimum.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= rebuilds <= k-2 for rebuilds in [min_rebuilds, max_rebuilds])
postconditions.description: The number of rebuilds cannot exceed k-2, as there are k-1 steps in the path and at most one rebuild per step (except the last).

postconditions.expression: lambda: (lambda compute: all(0 <= compute(min_rebuilds) <= compute(max_rebuilds) <= k-2 for compute in [min_rebuilds, max_rebuilds]))(lambda x: x)
postconditions.description: The computed min and max rebuilds must be valid for the given path and graph.
